text:
rachel: Heads-up: SOC wants to export a narrowed SIEM stream to a third-party forensics vendor (partner acct) for root-cause. Request asks for 14d indexed events + raw payloads for a 24h window. Key asks: cross-account KMS unwrap, short-lived STS role with external-id, and strict RBAC so vendor never gets direct KMS Decrypt. Can we do this without opening Decrypt to humans?

tim: We should absolutely avoid giving Decrypt to any human or vendor principal. pattern: export job writes objects encrypted with a data key, envelope-wrapped by our CMK. We grant a KMS Grant to the `kms-proxy` service in our account to perform Decrypt for that grant only, and the `kms-proxy` does cross-account export by assuming a partner role with external-id. Partner only gets the encrypted blob and assumes role to ingest; they never receive plaintext from our side.

anil: A few operational points: 1) ticket must include partner_arn and external_id; 2) STS assume-role duration <= 1h; 3) raw TTL 48h in partner storage after transfer, must be auto-deleted and partner must provide attest.

infra-bot: export job validation: required fields: ticket_id, requester, justification, from, to, partner_account, partner_role_arn, external_id, legal_approved. Missing fields -> reject.

rachel: thanks. legal: do we need extra signoff for cross-border transfers?

legal: yes. if export contains EU-resident PII or identifiers, require `legal_approved=true` and data transfer agreement signed. Add a pre-transfer scrub checklist and require vendor to run a signed ingest-check and return `ingest_attest` before we consider transfer complete.

anil: suggested flow: 1) infra-run generates data key and encrypts objects with `GenerateDataKey` -> stores encrypted data key with each object. 2) create KMS Grant scoped to `kms-proxy` with tag `ticket=XXX` and `expires=ts`. 3) kms-proxy reads encrypted objects, unwraps via grant, streams plaintext into an ephemeral archive, then calls partner STS assume-role (external-id) to push encrypted archive to partner bucket. 4) partner runs ingest-check -> writes `ingest_attest=PASSED|FAILED` to partner API and copies signed attest back to our s3://partner-attests/<ticket>/ signed by partner KMS.

tim: sample grant & policy snippet below (review):
```
# KMS Grant (pseudo)
GrantOperations: ["Decrypt","GenerateDataKey"]
GranteePrincipal: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/kms-proxy
Constraints: {"EncryptionContextEquals": {"ticket": "TICK-2026-01"}}
RetiringPrincipal: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/kms-admin
```

# Partner assume-role condition
```
{"Effect":"Allow","Action":"sts:AssumeRole","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/partner-ingest"},"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"sts:ExternalId":"<external-id-from-ticket>"}}}
```

anil: couple of guardrails: - Retire grant immediately after transfer completes - require audit event for every GrantCreate/GrantRetire with ticket metadata - require object sha256 recorded in audit sink - rotate data key if scrub fails.

rachel: RBAC changes: propose new `external_export_requester` role (can open ticket), and `external_export_operator` (infra ops, can run export CLI and create Grants). Humans cannot call KMS:Decrypt. KMS policies reserved to service principal and grant model.

infra-bot: enforcement checklist: - ticket has legal_approved if EU data - partner has signed DTA - external_id present and verified - transfer window <= 2h of assume-role - post-transfer attest present - raw retention_on_partner <= 48h.

legal: require a template clause for partner attestation: they must sign attest that they will delete raw by TTL and provide sha256 of deleted objects and deletion event id. Keep the deletion attest for 365d.

sec-lead: approve flow in principle. Additions: 1) require MFA for `external_export_operator` in prod; 2) require PR with terraform changes for grant creation and retire workflow; 3) add console link in ticket UI showing grant lifecycle and audit events.

tim: operational note: script will create grant via KMS CreateGrant API and tag request with `ticket` and `expires` in EncryptionContext. We'll call RetireGrant after partner attest. If attestation fails, rotate CMK and instruct partner to destroy.

rachel: i'll draft the ticket template and runbook and open PR for the RBAC/terraform changes. ticket template (example):
```
- ticket_id: EXT-2026-42
- requester: rachel@redwood.com
- justification: partner forensics ingestion for incident INC-2026-85
- from: 2026-02-10T00:00Z
- to: 2026-02-24T00:00Z
- partner_account: 999888777666
- partner_role_arn: arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/partner-ingest
- external_id: X8f7-abc
- legal_approved: true|false
- retention_partner_hours: 48
```

anil: LGTM. ping me on PR for the grant retire logic and audit sink wiring.

rachel: thanks all. i'll post PR link here once ready. closing unless objections. :lock:
